items.title: Jaylen Brown talks relationship with Jayson Tatum, Celtics fallout in intro presser
items.content:
LAS VEGAS, NV - JULY 11: Jaylen Brown attends a game between the Indiana Pacers and Philadelphia 76ers on July 11, 2026 at the Cox Pavilion in Las Vegas, Nevada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Mike Kirschbaum/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images	Just over a month after he was traded from the Celtics to Philadelphia, Jaylen Brown was officially introduced as a member of the 76ers on Thursday afternoon. 

“I’m excited to just be myself,” Brown said, sitting at the podium of the Francis J. Myers Recreation Center. “I think that’s one thing that I can promise the city and the organization and coaching staff that I’m coming every single day to be myself with my best foot forward. Be with my integrity, my mentality, and be with my capacity and my ability to win. We’ll figure out the X’s and O’s.”

In his introductory press conference, Brown fielded more than 20 minutes of questions from a press corps that included dozens of Philadelphia reporters, as well as a slew of Boston media members who made the trip to Pennsylvania to watch the longtime Celtic and former Finals MVP turn the page in his illustrious career. 

Brown touched on his excitement about the prospect of bringing a title to Philadelphia, and spoke candidly about how crazy of a summer it had been, getting traded to a rival franchise that eliminated the Celtics just a few weeks ago. 

He fielded questions about his eagerness to mentor rising sophomore VJ Edgecombe, who will be the youngest standout among a talented pool of stars. He spoke candidly about his excitement about the prospect of learning from LeBron James. And he shared how quickly franchise cornerstones Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid reached out to him after the trade. 

But, though Brown’s press conference mostly centered around the 76ers — and the organization’s title aspirations — he also reflected a bit on his Boston tenure. 

For one, he was asked which part of the trade process he felt was disrespectful, something he previously stated on the Twitch stream. 

“The whole process,” he said. 

“But to be honest, my mind is so focused on what’s in front of me. To be honest, I’m moving on. Maybe one day, I’ll share the details and how everything transpired and all the moving parts that took place in this. Obviously, it’s a lot of speculation. I feel no need to chime in on it because I’m focused on what’s important.”

items.title: Mavericks ‘very resistant’ to buyout for Klay Thompson due to Lakers, Heat interest
items.content:
DALLAS, TEXAS - APRIL 12: Klay Thompson #31 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates a three point shot against the Chicago Bulls during the first half at American Airlines Center on April 12, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the GettyImages License Agreement. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images	Positioned directly in the dog days of summer, it’s prime time for teams to bluff like crazy, which appears to be what the Mavericks are doing.

One of the latest developments this offseason is a potential Klay Thompson-Lakers pairing. The veteran sharpshooter was once a free agent target in a different era for the purple and gold. After changes in both Dallas and Los Angeles, he could be back on the market late this summer with the Lakers interested.

Entering the final year of his contract, Thompson is a prime buyout candidate. Teams are aware of this and are lining up for him, with the Lakers included among them.

However, Dallas is also aware of that interest and is definitely not bluffing that they’ll keep Thompson and trade him. For now, that is their stance, as reported by Jake Fischer on a recent Bleacher Report video (emphasis added).

“To this point, Dallas has not been looking to find a buyout agreement with Klay Thompson. He’s got one year left on a three-year, $51 million deal that he signed two seasons ago when he left the Golden State Warriors, the franchise he won four championships with, of course…Klay Thompson very nearly chose the Los Angeles Lakers with then LeBron James over joining Dallas originally to pair with Luka Doncic and where’s Luka Doncic right now? Of course, with the Lakers. There’s plenty of connective tissue there that makes sense here. The only thing is, the Mavericks have been very resistant, to my understanding, of actually moving forward and agreeing to a buyout with Klay Thompson. They believe this market that’s shaping up for him, the fact that there is some LA interest, the fact that there is Miami interest. There’s probably other places that have interest in Klay Thompson as well.”

This is always the silly portion of this process. The team pretends they’re not going to buy out a player and trade him because of the interest in the player. But the interest in the player only exists if they’re bought out. So a team has to pretend they won’t buy him out while no one gives them a trade proposal.

As things stand, Thompson seems set for a buyout. Whether the Lakers have interest from that point does remain in the air. They already have too many players on the roster before signing him and likely wouldn’t guarantee him more like a spot off the bench.

Miami, meanwhile, seems like a place that could offer him a bigger role. It also becomes a question of how much he wants to play in Los Angeles.

items.title: Jaylen Brown stresses that winning is his agenda with 76ers as questions about Jayson Tatum, Celtics follow him to Philly
items.content:
Jaylen Brown requested to hold his Philadelphia 76ers introductory news conference on Thursday at the Francis J. Myers Recreation Center in Southwest Philly as opposed to the franchise’s training facility across the Delaware River in Camden, New Jersey. Local children were invited to attend, and he stressed how he and his family are people who are rooted in the communities they occupy.

“That's where we hang our hat,” he said.

Yet as much as Brown emphasized his focus on his new home and his new squad, once a rival city and a rival team, he was peppered with questions about the place more than 300 miles away that he said a complicated goodbye to early this summer. Reporters, including a batch from Boston, inquired about the tumultuous end of his 10-season tenure with the Celtics, his relationship with longtime co-star Jayson Tatum and his latest feelings on the shocking trade that sent him down the East Coast to an organization he was taught to hate, essentially from the day he was drafted at 19 years old out of Cal.

Brown, 29, seemingly bit his tongue at times, wanting to, in his words, “move forward,” except it was impossible to totally ignore the drama that still surrounds him, a bit more than a month after he was dealt to the Sixers for a 36-year-old Paul George and four picks.

The existing tension was crystal clear when a reporter asked the five-time All-Star forward if this summer’s transaction will fuel him, similar to how he found motivation when he was left off Team USA’s roster for the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Brown, of course, now will face the Celtics routinely as part of a Sixers team also competing in the Atlantic Division. 

He chuckled to himself before saying, “Say that one more time.”

“You’re going to face them a couple times,” the reporter said.

“Just one day at a time,” Brown replied. “That’s all I got.”

Jaylen Brown on being fueled to face the Celtics, the sentiment he has, as he smiles and laughs, asks the reporter to repeat what she said: "Say it one more time".

Reporter: "You gonna face them a couple of times."

items.title: Jaylen Brown Says No Contact With Jayson Tatum Since Trade, But 'Nothing But Respect'
items.content:
Jaylen Brown addressed his relationship with former Boston Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum for the first time since being traded to the Philadelphia 76ers, saying the two have had little contact since the move but that he holds no resentment toward him.

"Not really," said Brown, when asked whether he and Tatum had spoken since the trade. "We won a championship together. So anybody that you won a championship, you would think that's what a brotherhood or a lifelong legacy would entail. Obviously there's ups and downs in any type of relationship for sure. But on my end, it's nothing but respect. Besides when he plays the Sixers, I hope he does well. But other than that, everything for me is just based in respect."

Brown made the comments during his introductory press conference Thursday in Philadelphia, where he addressed a range of topics tied to his abrupt departure from Boston after 10 seasons. He said he wasn't entirely surprised by the trade given how frequently his name had surfaced in trade discussions, though he expressed frustration with how the Celtics communicated the process.

"When I first got traded, I just threw my phone across the room," said Brown.

Brown said he has been in regular contact with his new Philadelphia teammates, including Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Joel Embiid and LeBron James, all of whom reached out following the trade. He also acknowledged the challenge of blending talented personalities on a new roster.

"Obviously it's a lot of guys with talent and egos," said Brown. "But to win, you got to be able to sacrifice, you got to be able to have trust and communicate. I want to come in transparent. I want to come in with my agenda on the table."

Brown declined to elaborate further on previous comments suggesting he felt disrespected by the Celtics' handling of trade discussions, saying he preferred to look ahead rather than revisit the details.

"To be honest, I'm moving on," said Brown. "Maybe one day you share the details of how everything transpired and all the moving parts that took place in this. Obviously it's a lot of speculation. I feel no need to chime in on it because I'm focused on what's in front of me."
